sanskrit: aihalaukikam īhante māṃsaśoṇitavardhanam pāralaukikakāryeṣu prasuptā bhṛśanāstikāḥ
english: Those hardened unbelievers strive only after worldly things that nourish flesh and blood, while toward the works that bear upon the world beyond they lie fast asleep.

sanskrit: dharmāya ye 'bhyasūyanti buddhimohānvitā narāḥ apathā gacchatāṃ teṣām anuyātāpi pīḍyate
english: As for the men, deluded in mind, who cavil at dharma, of those who walk the wrong road even one who merely follows after them comes to grief.

sanskrit: ye tu tuṣṭāḥ suniyatāḥ satyāgamaparāyaṇāḥ dharmyaṃ panthānam ārūḍhās tān upāssva ca pṛccha ca
english: But those who are content, well-controlled, devoted to the scripture of truth, who have mounted the path of dharma — attend upon them and question them.

sanskrit: upadhārya mataṃ teṣāṃ vṛddhānāṃ dharmadarśinām niyaccha parayā buddhyā cittam utpathagāmi vai
english: Having marked well the counsel of those elders who behold dharma, restrain with the highest understanding your mind that strays onto wrong paths.

sanskrit: adyakālikayā buddhyā dūre śva iti nirbhayāḥ sarvabhakṣā na paśyanti karmabhūmiṃ vicetasaḥ
english: With a mind fixed on the present hour, thinking "tomorrow is far off," fearless and devouring all things, the senseless do not see the field of works.

sanskrit: dharmaniḥśreṇim āsthāya kiṃ cit kiṃ cit samāruha kośakāravad ātmānaṃ veṣṭayan nāvabudhyase
english: Mounting the ladder of dharma, climb it rung by little rung. Like the silkworm that wraps itself round, you do not awaken to your own confinement.

sanskrit: nāstikaṃ bhinnamaryādaṃ kūlapātam ivāsthiram vāmataḥ kuru visrabdho naraṃ veṇum ivoddhatam
english: The unbeliever, who has broken every bound, unsteady as a collapsing riverbank, set him at your left without misgiving — a man arrogant as a reed shooting up.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca mṛtyuṃ ca pañcendriyajalāṃ nadīm nāvaṃ dhṛtimayīṃ kṛtvā janmadurgāṇi saṃtara
english: Across the river whose waters are desire, anger, and death, fed by the five senses, make for yourself a boat of steadfastness and cross over the strongholds of birth.

sanskrit: mṛtyunābhyāhate loke jarayā paripīḍite amoghāsu patantīṣu dharmayānena saṃtara
english: In a world struck down by death and oppressed by old age, while the unerring arrows fall, cross over by the vehicle of dharma.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhantaṃ ca śayānaṃ ca mṛtyur anveṣate yadā nirvṛtiṃ labhase kasmād akasmān mṛtyunāśitaḥ
english: Since death seeks out the man who stands and the man who lies down alike, from where will you find ease, when without warning you are undone by death?

sanskrit: saṃcinvānakam evainaṃ kāmānām avitṛptakam vṛkīvoraṇam āsādya mṛtyur ādāya gacchati
english: Even while he goes on heaping up, still unsated in his desires, death comes upon him as a she-wolf upon a lamb, seizes him, and is gone.

sanskrit: kramaśaḥ saṃcitaśikho dharmabuddhimayo mahān andhakāre praveṣṭavye dīpo yatnena dhāryatām
english: Let the great lamp whose flame is gathered step by step, fashioned of the resolve toward dharma, be held with care against the darkness that must be entered.

sanskrit: saṃpatan dehajālāni kadā cid iha mānuṣe brāhmaṇyaṃ labhate jantus tat putra paripālaya
english: Falling through the meshes of body after body, only now and then in the human state does a creature attain brahminhood; guard it well, my son.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya hi deho 'yaṃ na kāmārthāya jāyate iha kleśāya tapase pretya tv anupamaṃ sukham
english: For this body of the brahmin is not born for the sake of pleasure: here it is for hardship and austerity, but beyond, for happiness beyond compare.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyaṃ bahubhir avāpyate tapobhis; tal labdhvā na paripaṇena heḍitavyam svādhyāye tapasi dame ca nityayuktaḥ; kṣemārthī kuśalaparaḥ sadā yatasva
english: Brahminhood is won by many austerities; having gained it, one must not make light of it for any wage. Ever yoked to recitation, to austerity, and to self-restraint, seeking your welfare and intent on the good, strive always.

sanskrit: avyaktaprakṛtir ayaṃ kalāśarīraḥ; sūkṣmātmā kṣaṇatruṭiśo nimeṣaromā ṛtvāsyaḥ samabalaśuklakṛṣṇanetro; māṃsāṅgo dravati vayohayo narāṇām
english: Unmanifest in its nature, bodied in fractions, subtle of self, made of moments and instants, its hairs the blinks of an eye, its mouth the seasons, its eyes the bright and dark halves equal in force, its limbs of flesh — the horse of men's lifetime gallops on.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā prasṛtam ajasram ugravegaṃ; gacchantaṃ satatam ihāvyapekṣamāṇam cakṣus te yadi na parapraṇetṛneyaṃ; dharme te bhavatu manaḥ paraṃ niśamya
english: Seeing it loosed, unceasing, fierce in its speed, going on forever here without a backward glance — if your eye is not one to be led by another's leading, then, having grasped the highest, let your mind rest upon dharma.

sanskrit: ye 'mī tu pracalitadharmakāmavṛttāḥ; krośantaḥ satatam aniṣṭasaṃprayogāḥ kliśyante parigatavedanāśarīrā; bahvībhiḥ subhṛśam adharmavāsanābhiḥ
english: But those whose conduct has slipped from dharma into craving, forever crying out, yoked to what they would not have, are afflicted, their bodies wholly encompassed by pain, harried sorely by the many residues of unrighteousness.

sanskrit: rājā dharmaparaḥ sadā śubhagoptā; samīkṣya sukṛtināṃ dadhāti lokān bahuvidham api carataḥ pradiśati; sukham anupagataṃ niravadyam
english: The king devoted to dharma, ever the guardian of good, after due regard bestows their worlds upon the doers of good; and to one who fares in manifold ways he allots a happiness unattained before, and blameless.

sanskrit: śvāno bhīṣaṇāyomukhāni vayāṃsi; vaḍagṛdhrakulapakṣiṇāṃ ca saṃghāḥ narāṃ kadane rudhirapā guruvacana;nudam uparataṃ viśasanti
english: Dogs with dread iron jaws, and birds, and the flocking hosts of herons and vultures, drinkers of blood, in the slaughter of men tear apart the one who, ceasing to heed, has spurned his teacher's word.

sanskrit: maryādā niyatāḥ svayaṃbhuvā ya ihemāḥ; prabhinatti daśaguṇā manonugatvāt nivasati bhṛśam asukhaṃ pitṛviṣaya;vipinam avagāhya sa pāpaḥ
english: He who, following the bent of his mind, shatters tenfold these bounds laid down here by the Self-Born — that sinner dwells in deep misery, plunged into the wilderness of the realm of the fathers.

sanskrit: yo lubdhaḥ subhṛśaṃ priyānṛtaś ca manuṣyaḥ; satatanikṛtivañcanāratiḥ syāt upanidhibhir asukhakṛt sa paramanirayago; bhṛśam asukham anubhavati duṣkṛtakarmā
english: The man who is wholly greedy and loves falsehood, who takes ceaseless delight in cheating and deceit, who works misery with deposits entrusted to him — that doer of evil deeds goes to the deepest hell and there suffers misery without end.

sanskrit: uṣṇāṃ vaitaraṇīṃ mahānadīm; avagāḍho 'sipatravanabhinnagātraḥ paraśuvanaśayo nipatito; vasati ca mahāniraye bhṛśārtaḥ
english: Plunged into the scalding Vaitaraṇī, that great river, his limbs torn in the forest of sword-leaf trees, fallen to lie in the forest of axes, he dwells in the great hell, sore-stricken.

sanskrit: mahāpadāni katthase na cāpy avekṣase param cirasya mṛtyukārikām anāgatāṃ na budhyase
english: You boast of mighty exploits, yet you do not look to what lies beyond; you do not perceive the long-deferred summoner, death, until it has come.

sanskrit: prayāsyatāṃ kim āsyate samutthitaṃ mahad bhayam atipramāthi dāruṇaṃ sukhasya saṃvidhīyatām
english: For those who must depart, why this sitting still? A great terror has risen up, crushing and dreadful: see to your own well-being.

sanskrit: purā mṛtaḥ praṇīyase yamasya mṛtyuśāsanāt tad antikāya dāruṇaiḥ prayatnam ārjave kuru
english: Before, struck dead, you are led away by Yama's death-decree, against that drawing-near make harsh effort toward uprightness.

sanskrit: purā samūlabāndhavaṃ prabhur haraty aduḥkhavit taveha jīvitaṃ yamo na cāsti tasya vārakaḥ
english: Before the Lord who knows no sorrow carries off your life here together with kin and root — and there is none to hold him back — act.

sanskrit: purā vivāti māruto yamasya yaḥ puraḥsaraḥ puraika eva nīyase kuruṣva sāṃparāyikam
english: Before the wind that is Yama's herald blows, before you are led off, you alone — make provision for the journey beyond.

sanskrit: purā sahikka eva te pravāti māruto 'ntakaḥ purā ca vibhramanti te diśo mahābhayāgame
english: Before the wind of the Ender blows upon you with the death-rattle, and before, at the coming of the great terror, the quarters reel about you — act.

sanskrit: smṛtiś ca saṃnirudhyate purā taveha putraka samākulasya gacchataḥ samādhim uttamaṃ kuru
english: Before your memory is choked off here, my son, and you depart in utter confusion — achieve the highest concentration.

sanskrit: kṛtākṛte śubhāśubhe pramādakarmaviplute smaran purā na tapyase nidhatsva kevalaṃ nidhim
english: Before you grieve, recalling the good and evil done and left undone, ruined by the works of heedlessness — lay up the one true treasure.

sanskrit: purā jarā kalevaraṃ vijarjarīkaroti te balāṅgarūpahāriṇī nidhatsva kevalaṃ nidhim
english: Before old age, robber of strength and limb and form, wears your frame to ruin — lay up the one true treasure.

sanskrit: purā śarīram antako bhinatti rogasāyakaiḥ prasahya jīvitakṣaye tapo mahat samācara
english: Before the Ender, with the arrows of disease, by main force splits your body at the wasting of life — practice great austerity.

sanskrit: purā vṛkā bhayaṃkarā manuṣyadehagocarāḥ abhidravanti sarvato yatasva puṇyaśīlane
english: Before the dread wolves whose range is the human body rush upon you from every side — strive in the cultivation of merit.

sanskrit: purāndhakāram ekako 'nupaśyasi tvarasva vai purā hiraṇmayān nagān nirīkṣase 'drimūrdhani
english: Before, alone, you behold the darkness, make haste indeed; before you gaze upon the golden trees on the mountain's crest — act.

sanskrit: purā kusaṃgatāni te suhṛnmukhāś ca śatravaḥ vicālayanti darśanād ghaṭasva putra yat param
english: Before bad company and foes wearing the faces of friends shake you from your vision — strive, my son, for what is highest.

sanskrit: dhanasya yasya rājato bhayaṃ na cāsti caurataḥ mṛtaṃ ca yan na muñcati samarjayasva tad dhanam
english: That wealth which fears nothing from the king nor from the thief, and which does not forsake even the dead — gather that wealth.

sanskrit: na tatra saṃvibhajyate svakarmabhiḥ parasparam yad eva yasya yautakaṃ tad eva tatra so 'śnute
english: There no man shares with another out of his own deeds; whatever is each one's own portion, that alone he enjoys there.

sanskrit: paratra yena jīvyate tad eva putra dīyatām dhanaṃ yad akṣayaṃ dhruvaṃ samarjayasva tat svayam
english: That by which one lives in the world beyond — that, my son, is what should be given. Gather for yourself, with your own hand, the wealth that is imperishable and sure.

sanskrit: na yāvad eva pacyate mahājanasya yāvakam apakva eva yāvake purā praṇīyase tvara
english: As long as the gruel of the great host is not yet cooked — while that gruel is still raw — before you are led away, make haste.

sanskrit: na mātṛpitṛbāndhavā na saṃstutaḥ priyo janaḥ anuvrajanti saṃkaṭe vrajantam ekapātinam
english: Neither mother, father, and kin, nor any well-known and beloved person follow after him who passes through the strait, going down alone.

sanskrit: yad eva karma kevalaṃ svayaṃ kṛtaṃ śubhāśubham tad eva tasya yautakaṃ bhavaty amutra gacchataḥ
english: Whatever deed, good or evil, one has done by oneself alone — that, and that only, becomes his portion as he goes to the world beyond.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaratnasaṃcayāḥ śubhāśubhena saṃcitāḥ na tasya dehasaṃkṣaye bhavanti kāryasādhakāḥ
english: Hoards of gold and jewels, amassed by fair means or foul, do not, at the dissolution of his body, serve to accomplish his purpose.

sanskrit: paratragāmikasya te kṛtākṛtasya karmaṇaḥ na sākṣir ātmanā samo nṛṇām ihāsti kaś cana
english: Of your deeds done and left undone that travel with you to the world beyond, there is among men here no witness equal to your own self.

sanskrit: manuṣyadehaśūnyakaṃ bhavaty amutra gacchataḥ prapaśya buddhicakṣuṣā pradṛśyate hi sarvataḥ
english: For him who goes to the world beyond, the human body becomes void and empty; behold this with the eye of understanding, for so it is shown on every side.

sanskrit: ihāgnisūryavāyavaḥ śarīram āśritās trayaḥ ta eva tasya sākṣiṇo bhavanti dharmadarśinaḥ
english: Here three — Agni, Sūrya, and Vāyu — dwell within the body; these very ones become his witnesses, the beholders of his dharma.

sanskrit: yathāniśeṣu sarvataḥspṛśatsu sarvadāriṣu prakāśagūḍhavṛttiṣu svadharmam eva pālaya
english: While they pass through every night, touching all things, rending all things, working now openly and now in secret — guard your own dharma.

sanskrit: anekapāripanthike virūparaudrarakṣite svam eva karma rakṣyatāṃ svakarma tatra gacchati
english: On a road beset by many highwaymen, watched over by misshapen and terrible guards, let one's own deed be one's safeguard, for it is one's own deed that goes thither.

sanskrit: na tatra saṃvibhajyate svakarmaṇā parasparam yathākṛtaṃ svakarmajaṃ tad eva bhujyate phalam
english: There no man shares with another out of his own deed; the fruit, born of one's own deed and shaped just as the deed was done — that alone is tasted.

sanskrit: yathāpsarogaṇāḥ phalaṃ sukhaṃ maharṣibhiḥ saha tathāpnuvanti karmato vimānakāmagāminaḥ
english: As the throngs of apsarases, together with the great sages, attain their fruit and their joy, so men, by their deeds, attain it — borne in flying chariots at their will.

sanskrit: yatheha yat kṛtaṃ śubhaṃ vipāpmabhiḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ tad āpnuvanti mānavās tathā viśuddhayonayaḥ
english: Whatever good is done here by the sinless and the perfected of soul, that the men of purified birth likewise attain.

sanskrit: prajāpateḥ salokatāṃ bṛhaspateḥ śatakratoḥ vrajanti te parāṃ gatiṃ gṛhasthadharmasetubhiḥ
english: By the causeways of the householder's dharma they go to the supreme goal — to a shared world with Prajāpati, with Bṛhaspati, and with the Hundred-Sacrificer.

sanskrit: sahasraśo 'py anekaśaḥ pravaktum utsahāmahe abuddhimohanaṃ punaḥ prabhur vinā na yāvakam
english: A thousandfold, in manifold ways, I am eager to declare it; yet without the Lord, the gruel of folly that deludes the mind is not undone.

sanskrit: gatā dviraṣṭavarṣatā dhruvo 'si pañcaviṃśakaḥ kuruṣva dharmasaṃcayaṃ vayo hi te 'tivartate
english: Your twice-eight years are gone; soon, surely, you will be twenty-five. Make your store of dharma, for your lifetime slips past you.

sanskrit: purā karoti so 'ntakaḥ pramādagomukhaṃ damam yathāgṛhītam utthitaṃ tvarasva dharmapālane
english: Before that Ender lays his curb, whose mouth gapes upon the heedless — even as it was grasped, so it has risen up — make haste in the keeping of dharma.

sanskrit: yadā tvam eva pṛṣṭhatas tvam agrato gamiṣyasi tathā gatiṃ gamiṣyataḥ kim ātmanā pareṇa vā
english: When you yourself shall go behind, and you yourself before, what use are self or other to one bound on that road?

sanskrit: yad ekapātināṃ satāṃ bhavaty amutra gacchatām bhayeṣu sāṃparāyikaṃ nidhatsva taṃ mahānidhim
english: That which serves the good who go down alone to the world beyond — that great treasure for the journey amid its terrors — lay it up.

sanskrit: sakūlamūlabāndhavaṃ prabhur haraty asaṅgavān na santi yasya vārakāḥ kuruṣva dharmasaṃnidhim
english: The Lord, unhindered, carries off a man with his line, his root, and his kin, and there are none who can stop him; therefore lay up a store of dharma.

sanskrit: idaṃ nidarśanaṃ mayā taveha putra saṃmatam svadarśanānumānataḥ pravarṇitaṃ kuruṣva tat
english: This teaching, my son, that I hold fitting for you here, set forth from my own insight and inference — act upon it.

sanskrit: dadhāti yaḥ svakarmaṇā dhanāni yasya kasya cit abuddhimohajair guṇaiḥ śataika eva yujyate
english: He who by his own deed bestows his wealth on this man or that, through qualities born of folly and delusion, finds but one reward in a hundred.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ samartham astu te prakurvataḥ śubhāḥ kriyāḥ tad eva tatra darśanaṃ kṛtajñam arthasaṃhitam
english: Let your sacred learning be made to bear fruit as you perform good works; that alone is the wisdom there which knows its debts and is joined to true aim.

sanskrit: nibandhanī rajjur eṣā yā grāme vasato ratiḥ chittvaināṃ sukṛto yānti naināṃ chindanti duṣkṛtaḥ
english: This delight in dwelling in the village is the tethering rope; the doers of good cut it and depart, but the doers of evil cannot cut it.

sanskrit: kiṃ te dhanena kiṃ bandhubhis te; kiṃ te putraiḥ putraka yo mariṣyasi ātmānam anviccha guhāṃ praviṣṭaṃ; pitāmahās te kva gatāś ca sarve
english: What is your wealth to you, what your kinsmen, what your sons, my son, you who must die? Seek out the Self that has entered into the cave of the heart. And your grandfathers — where have they all gone?

sanskrit: śvaḥkāryam adya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇikam ko hi tad veda kasyādya mṛtyusenā nivekṣyate
english: Let tomorrow's task be done today, and the afternoon's in the morning; for who knows whose, and on what day, the army of death will come knocking?

sanskrit: anugamya śmaśānāntaṃ nivartantīha bāndhavāḥ agnau prakṣipya puruṣaṃ jñātayaḥ suhṛdas tathā
english: Having followed as far as the edge of the burning ground, the kinsmen here turn back, casting the man into the fire — both kin and friends alike.

sanskrit: nāstikān niranukrośān narān pāpamatau sthitān vāmataḥ kuru viśrabdhaṃ paraṃ prepsur atandritaḥ
english: The unbelievers, the pitiless, men fixed in evil intent — set them at your left without misgiving, you who, untiring, seek what is highest.

sanskrit: evam abhyāhate loke kālenopanipīḍite sumahad dhairyam ālambya dharmaṃ sarvātmanā kuru
english: While the world is thus struck down and pressed hard by Time, lay hold of a very great steadfastness and practice dharma with your whole soul.

sanskrit: athemaṃ darśanopāyaṃ samyag yo vetti mānavaḥ samyak sa dharmaṃ kṛtveha paratra sukham edhate
english: And the man who rightly knows this way of insight, having here done dharma aright, thrives in happiness in the world beyond.

sanskrit: na dehabhede maraṇaṃ vijānatāṃ; na ca praṇāśaḥ svanupālite pathi dharmaṃ hi yo vardhayate sa paṇḍito; ya eva dharmāc cyavate sa muhyati
english: For those who truly know, the breaking of the body is not death, nor is there annihilation when the path is well kept; he who makes dharma grow is the wise one, while he who falls away from dharma is the deluded.

sanskrit: prayuktayoḥ karmapathi svakarmaṇoḥ; phalaṃ prayoktā labhate yathāvidhi nihīnakarmā nirayaṃ prapadyate; triviṣṭapaṃ gacchati dharmapāragaḥ
english: Of one's own two kinds of deed set going upon the road of action, the doer reaps the fruit according to law: the man of base deeds comes to hell, while he who has crossed to the far shore of dharma goes to the triple heaven.

sanskrit: sopānabhūtaṃ svargasya mānuṣyaṃ prāpya durlabham tathātmānaṃ samādadhyād bhraśyeta na punar yathā
english: Having gained the hard-won human state, which is the stairway to heaven, one should so compose oneself that one does not fall away again.

sanskrit: yasya notkrāmati matiḥ svargamārgānusāriṇī tam āhuḥ puṇyakarmāṇam aśocyaṃ mitrabāndhavaiḥ
english: He whose mind, faithful to the path to heaven, does not stray from it — him they call a doer of meritorious deeds, one not to be mourned by friends and kin.

sanskrit: yasya nopahatā buddhir niścayeṣv avalambate svarge kṛtāvakāśasya tasya nāsti mahad bhayam
english: He whose unmarred understanding rests firm in its resolves, who has made his place secure in heaven — for him there is no great terror.

sanskrit: tapovaneṣu ye jātās tatraiva nidhanaṃ gatāḥ teṣām alpataro dharmaḥ kāmabhogam ajānatām
english: Those who are born in the groves of austerity and there meet their death — their dharma is the lesser, since they have never known the enjoyment of desire.

sanskrit: yas tu bhogān parityajya śarīreṇa tapaś caret na tena kiṃ cin na prāptaṃ tan me bahumataṃ phalam
english: But he who, having renounced pleasures, practices austerity with his body — by him there is nothing that is not attained; that, in my judgment, is the high fruit.

sanskrit: mātāpitṛsahasrāṇi putradāraśatāni ca anāgatāny atītāni kasya te kasya vā vayam
english: Thousands of mothers and fathers, and hundreds of sons and wives, are yet to come and have already passed away. Whose are they, and whose are we?

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ bhavatā kāryaṃ na kāryaṃ tava tair api svakṛtais tāni yātāni bhavāṃś caiva gamiṣyati
english: You have no business with them, nor they any with you; they have gone, each by his own deeds, and you too shall go.

sanskrit: iha loke hi dhaninaḥ paro 'pi svajanāyate svajanas tu daridrāṇāṃ jīvatām eva naśyati
english: For in this world even a stranger acts as kin to the rich man, while the very kinsmen of the poor desert them while they yet live.

sanskrit: saṃcinoty aśubhaṃ karma kalatrāpekṣayā naraḥ tataḥ kleśam avāpnoti paratreha tathaiva ca
english: A man heaps up evil deeds out of regard for wife and household, and thereby comes to suffering, both in the world beyond and here as well.

sanskrit: paśya tvaṃ chidrabhūtaṃ hi jīvalokaṃ svakarmaṇā tat kuruṣva tathā putra kṛtsnaṃ yat samudāhṛtam
english: See for yourself how the world of the living is riddled with holes by one's own deeds; therefore, my son, do in full all that has been declared.
